prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on the recent price trend: the share price is 21.1% higher than a year ago. Also in its favour: over the past year the share did 23.9 percentage points better than the Nifty 50; the share price is close to its 52-week high; and profit grew 13% compared with a year earlier. Other areas on this side: growth, risk, the balance sheet.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: free cash flow for the last financial year was negative: the business spent more than it generated. Also against it: return on capital employed is only 7.3%, a weak return on the money in the business; profit shrank 2.0% a year on average over three years; and quality scores only 17 of 100 against the comparison pool. Other areas on this side: the quality of the business, what the price asks for the earnings, the balance sheet.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 7 points in favour and 9 against give more points against. The pool score is 40 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with high confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
